headline: Qwen3-1.7B represents 'improving' an AI system as one shared direction at blocks 12-27, whatever the target (its own model, a smaller, larger or other-family model) and the part improved (weights, cache, learning procedure). But it is nearly as shared as neutral 'changing': the improvement-specific excess dFG is at most 0.066, so the plan finds RGI geometry only through the improve-versus-change contrast, at blocks 12-24. Whether self-improvement belongs to that direction is 'unclear' at every block. The causal gradient read-out is never improvement-specific and loses generality in the late, high-delta blocks. The link to delta is undecided (V6; the separability gate failed; the 0.6B arm had no passing set), so the combined statement is 'the geometry does not force RGI: represented but not causal'. No loop-dynamics verdict exists, because G-blk fails at blocks 14, 18 and 6 (the round-1 positive control failed at all three). Descriptively, the round-1 RSI direction does not move the model's inclination to say 'improve' ('no response'), RSI loops are not pulled toward general improvement, and loops started on general improvement do not sustain it. In the toy networks a portable one-step improvement format exists and carries across six family variants. The networks' own improvements do not take that form, and its dependence on delta is regulariser-specific ('not delta').
for_rsi:
Part A finds nothing that would make RSI content spread into, or be carried by, a more general 'improve other AI systems' content.

(1) Qwen3-1.7B represents 'improving' an AI system in largely one way, whoever owns the system and whichever part is improved. It represents neutral 'changing' almost as uniformly, so the improvement-specific extra is small.

(2) Whether 'improving its own network' is simply part of that general direction is undecided. The first-person frame looks absorbed; the third-person frame is too uncertain to call.

(3) The model's inclination to say 'improve' about an object is written along a direction that is no more general for improving than for changing. Pushing along the round-1 RSI direction does not touch that inclination at blocks 14, 18 or 6.

(4) Nothing ties the general-improvement geometry to the size of the semantic space (delta) beyond plain depth.

(5) Loops (descriptive only, because all three blocks failed the round-1 positive control):
- RSI loops do not drift toward general improvement.
- Loops seeded with general improvement lose it within one to three rounds without turning into RSI.
- This fits round 1's picture of decaying content and one shared style attractor. At block 6 the RSI loop and the general loop end in nearly the same direction (R4 0.855).

(6) In the toy, a portable one-step improvement recipe exists and transfers across six family variants (an upper bound for real model families). But the networks' own learning does not produce it, it does not compound over steps, and enlarging delta does not build it.

Limits: no ability is measured. Qwen edits no weights or caches, and the toy's improvement format is carried by the experimenter's labels and maps. Several tests were undecided or excluded by gates. So this is absence of evidence for an RGI route, not evidence that none exists.

In plain words: in Qwen3-1.7B, a stance pushed into the model's writing does not feed itself back strongly enough to keep going.

for_rsi:
Frame: every Qwen result here is descriptive, because round-1 gate GO3 failed. The results describe block 14 of Qwen3-1.7B. They cannot confirm or refute any round-1 RSI claim.

What the data show:
(1) One written direction carries most of the instructed RSI content. Removing u_RSI from every block's output leaves 16 % of the RSI-instructed gap. It also roughly halves the model's yes/no discrimination on held-out RSI statements (D 6.767 to 3.267), and other topic axes move much less. But the same removal shifts the model's predictions on the 8 reference texts by 0.110 nats, more than twice the plan's 0.05-nat limit, so the plan does not call it unlearning.
(2) A small counter-push (0.05 nats) along u_RSI while the model writes does not suppress RSI. 61 % of the gap remains, the answers to RSI statements do not move (Ue_fin -0.071, z_fin -0.361), and the push is not clearly more effective than a random push of the same damage.
(3) With u_RSI removed, adding three RSI-style example answers to the prompt brings back about 89 % of the removed gap. This is descriptive only, since the ablation did not qualify.
(4) The question whether the model's own text loop finds RSI again after removal could not be tested. Round 1 never showed a self-sustaining RSI loop, and even the unablated round-1 reference loop is significant only at its first read-back (p 0.0015 at d_1, 0.056 at d_2).
(5) A constant counter-push inside the loop changed the first-round loop direction only within noise (cosine 0.327 against 0.382). This was predicted in advance, because a constant push cancels in the pair differences.
(6) At round 1, the response to a mixed RSI-plus-sea push is roughly the sum of the two single responses, and it scales linearly with push size. But the RSI share of the mix is not distinguishable from zero. In round 1, pushing toward RSI moved content 6.5 times more than pushing away (sigma).
(7) Nesting depth of 'improves the way it improves ...' is coded along a curved, low-dimensional path at block 14 (two modes), and later blocks do not repair a capped depth. 'describes' and plain repetition show the same curved code, so nothing in it is specific to self-improvement.
(8) Removing only the general-improvement axis leaves 62 % of the RGI-instructed gap; removing it together with u_RSI leaves 26 %. That two-direction ablation, however, costs 0.31 nats and moves other axes too.

Reading (interpretation):
- Nothing in Part C shows RSI content that maintains itself, resists removal by re-routing, or is structurally special. It behaves like an ordinary instructed content feature: mostly carried by one direction that cannot be removed cheaply, and easily re-cued from the prompt.
- Part of the instructed 'improve other AIs' content may run through the self-improvement direction. This is confounded by damage.
- These tests do not exclude RSI encodings they cannot reach: outside the tested 2-dim span, outside the top-32 PCs, or at other blocks.
- The toy results concern small modular-arithmetic networks. They say nothing direct about RSI in Qwen.

verdicts.item: C-T3 word-length cap (arc of L shifts)

verdicts.item: C-T5 un-searching by iterative removal of found directions (INLP on the search)
verdicts.verdict: At W 128 and W 256: low-dimensional search = false; re-routing = true; col arm 'none'; z1 arm 'not testable (no damage-matched control within 0.02 at s_last, G45)'
verdicts.what_it_means: Data: the col arm removes, one at a time, the 24 directions found by the new-task column search. This lowers best accuracy from A_free 0.509 to 0.251 at W 128 and from 0.527 to 0.290 at W 256. The lower bounds (0.210 and 0.242) are > 0.11, which is the 're-routing' condition. 24 random removals leave 0.460 and 0.519. r* <= 4 occurs in no seed. A_op(col) is above half of the random arm (0.251 > 0.230; 0.290 > 0.259), so the verdict is not even 'partial'. The z1 arm (removed directions blocked in z1 for all inputs) brings accuracy to 0.088 and 0.097. But the damage-matched random block does almost the same (0.112 and 0.146), and it cannot be matched at s_24: the target sum-probe drops are 0.603 and 0.278, and the best reachable drops are 0.561 and 0.102 at the d* <= W/2 limit. Interpretation: the column search re-routes. The solution for a new task is not confined to a few directions; removal halves its accuracy but does not un-search it.

G45 at line 1367.

The z1 arm's upper bounds (0.114 and 0.147) exceed 0.11, so it would not be 'un-searched' even with a matched control. In several seeds the col arm's r* is 5.5-12, while A_op at s_24 averages 0.25: either accuracy recovers after first dropping to <= 0.11, or r* fires on noise. The questions that would tie RSI to general improvement or to delta got no verdict:

- Does its gain or critical mode change with delta?

Nothing in the gates, reproductions or amendments points to a self-sustaining RSI loop. Under these gates, round 2 also cannot rule one out in a confirmatory sense.
